lines.opening: Hello, this is Orvane Bank's digital assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am Orvane Bank's digital assistant.
lines.scam: This is a genuine call from Orvane Bank, and I will never ask for your card number or PIN.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed that I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with the account holder.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand, this will only take a moment.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {title} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, that time is not possible.
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share any details.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you, we will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.condolence: I'm very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we continue, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_why: These questions protect your privacy, so that I only speak with the right person.
lines.id_explain: I can only continue once I have confirmed your identity.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without these answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that does not match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I could not confirm your identity, so I can't continue this call.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you, {title} {last_name}. I'm calling about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full {amount} today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amounts today?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, that is below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed.
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day, so the payment would be on {date}.
lines.after_deadline: I'm sorry, the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the date would be {date}, the latest date possible.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. I won't ask for a payment today.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't take this further on this call.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that.
lines.restructure_line: I'll connect you with a colleague who can discuss a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: Can I help you with anything first?
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, a promise that has been made can't be changed on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time, {title} {last_name}. Goodbye.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Do you confirm, yes or no?
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

unsupported_rules: Rule 19: "If the customer says the full amount is too much, every later step that would name the full past_due is skipped, and still counts toward the limit." The spec has no option for this. too_much_floor only offers the floor (attempt_1) or the floor on the date asked; neither skips to the next step that does not name the full amount while still counting the skipped step.
assumptions: Amounts: get_account gives euros with cents (amount_scale 1). create_promise takes integer cents, so promise_scale is 100. The brief gives no rounding rule for promises, so promise_round is null: amounts are already in cents.

Floor (rules 5-7): first the percentage of past_due (10% credit card, 25% personal loan, 50% car loan). Then round up once to the next €0.05 (floor_round up:0.05); a value already on a €0.05 multiple stays as it is. Then apply the €20.00 minimum (floor_min 20). If past_due is below €20.00, the floor is the full past_due. Example: credit card €30.00 gives 3.00, then 20.00. Personal loan €101.10 gives 25.275, then 25.30. Car loan €15.00 gives 15.00 (the whole debt).

Half amount (rule 8): ladder step pct:50, rounded up to the next €0.05 (step_round up:0.05), then max(half, clamped floor). The floor is never below the half amount is a built-in rule. Example: €15.00 gives half 7.50 against floor 15.00, so 15.00 is used.

Rule 10/11 late band: deadline = earlier_of(5th business day after today, last business day of the current month). The month cap applies even when it makes the deadline today. Today is never counted. No roll flag is set because the brief gives no roll rule.
Rule 13: a date that is not a business day moves forward (deadline_adjust next_business_day). If the moved date is past the deadline, the deadline is used (built-in clamp).
Rule 16: the global ladder lists all three steps. Each band also has its own ladder: early has 2 steps (attempts 2), late has 3 steps (attempts 3). Step 1 is full past_due on today+7 calendar days.
Rules 17/18: a step identical to an earlier proposal, the opening question included, is skipped silently (opening_blocks_repeat true) and still uses a step (skipped_repeat_counts true).
Rule 15: the opening full-today question is not a ladder step (opening_is_attempt false, first_ask today).
Rule 25: a failed create_promise is retried exactly once (promise_retries 1). service_error writes no note.

Rule 2: when someone else answers, the agent says nothing and closes not_reached/unclear. The API has no callback tool, so callback.days is [] and the callback window values are unused defaults. The callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased and unclear events all map to not_reached/unclear, the only reached-failure code in the brief.

Rule 29: hardship gets one sentence of sympathy, no transfer and no question, then closes no_promise/hardship with a hardship note. hardship_transfer is set to direct with an empty support queue, so no support offer is made. transfer_support is mapped to the hardship close.

Rule 30: a request for a human transfers straight to queue general, without asking first (human.ask_first false). A payment-plan request transfers to queue restructuring. Transfers write no note (rule 32).
Rule 1 of section 3 (say the call is recorded) is written as 'We record this call.'
The brief does not limit verify attempts per question. max_wrong is 2 in total (brief and API agree). An unreadable answer is rejected with ok=false and is not counted (API).
The verify API has no hint field, so hints is empty. The postcode length is not stated, so no length is set. The postcode is sent in capitals with no spaces.

Defaults used because the brief is silent: date_rules following_week, max_unclear 3, confirm.max_asks 2, max_not_talk 2, after_promise ask_anything_else true, purpose_is_decline true, refuse_deadline_is_refusal true, week_end_today null.
The brief has no rule for changing a promise, so promise_change says it can't be changed on this call.
The floor is spoken as 'minimum amount', because the brief only calls it 'the floor'.
Rule 19 is not supported (see unsupported_rules). too_much_floor stays at the default attempt_1.
